primary_source.title: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

policy_note: Common Core is used by MathBridge as a US comparison baseline only. It is not a single national US curriculum and state standards may differ.

expectations: Solve addition and subtraction situations within 20 with unknowns in different positions.
Use properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction as strategies.
Develop fluency within 20 and fluency within 10 using strategies such as counting on, making ten and decomposing to ten.
Add within 100 in selected two-digit cases using concrete models or drawings and place-value-based strategies, related to a written method.

multiplication_division.status: not yet a formal grade-level domain
multiplication_division.preparation: No formal multiplication/division standards; foundations are built through equal groups and repeated structures in later Grade 2.

expectations: Solve one- and two-step addition/subtraction problems within 100.
Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies and know one-digit sums from memory by the end of the grade.
Fluently add and subtract within 100 using place value, properties of operations and/or inverse relationships.
Add and subtract within 1000 using concrete models or drawings and place-value-based strategies; relate the strategy to a written method and explain why it works.
addition_subtraction.important_difference: Grade 2 explicitly expects strategy explanation and written-method connections, but not the standard algorithm as the endpoint.

expectations: Work with odd/even structure by pairing and equal addends.
Use repeated addition to find totals in rectangular arrays up to 5 by 5.
Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
addition_subtraction.note: A range of algorithms may be used; the standard algorithm is not yet mandated.

expectations: Interpret multiplication as equal groups and division as both sharing and grouping.
Solve multiplication/division problems within 100 using equal groups, arrays and measurement contexts.
Use properties of multiplication and the multiplication–division relationship.
Fluently multiply and divide within 100; know products of two one-digit numbers from memory by the end of Grade 3.
Multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of 10 using place value and properties.
Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
Multiply up to four-digit by one-digit and two-digit by two-digit whole numbers using place-value/property-based strategies.
Illustrate and explain multiplication using equations, rectangular arrays and/or area models.
Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors using place value, properties and/or multiplication–division relationships.
Illustrate and explain division using equations, arrays and/or area models.
multiplication_division.important_difference: Grade 4 requires the standard algorithm for addition/subtraction, but deliberately continues conceptual/representational strategies for multi-digit multiplication and division.

expectations: Add and subtract decimals to hundredths using concrete models or drawings and place-value/property-based strategies, relating strategies to written methods and explaining reasoning.
Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

Find quotients with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors using place-value/property-based strategies and/or multiplication–division relationships, explaining with equations, arrays and/or area models.
Multiply and divide decimals to hundredths using models/drawings and reasoning connected to written methods.

addition_subtraction.status: whole-number and decimal fluency assumed from earlier grades; arithmetic is applied in rational-number and algebraic contexts

multiplication_division.status: multi-digit whole-number division reaches the standard-algorithm fluency endpoint in Grade 6 in Common Core progression
multiplication_division.teacher_note: MathBridge should distinguish this from England, where formal long division appears explicitly in Year 6, and from any Chinese textbook placement that must be edition-verified before claiming exact grade equivalence.

mathbridge_interpretation.core_pattern: Common Core deliberately separates conceptual/strategic development from the point at which the standard algorithm becomes mandatory. Addition/subtraction reaches that endpoint in Grade 4; multi-digit multiplication in Grade 5; division later.
mathbridge_interpretation.comparison_warning: Standards specify endpoints, not a mandated daily teaching sequence or textbook method.
